By the end of A Storm of Swords the Stark cause lay in ruins. Robb Stark and his mother Catelyn were butchered at the treacherous Red Wedding. The boy king Joffrey was poisoned at his own wedding feast; his brother Tommen was crowned in his place, with Cersei Lannister ruling as regent. Tyrion Lannister, wrongly condemned for Joffrey's murder, killed his father Tywin and fled into exile. Jaime Lannister returned to the capital maimed, having lost his sword hand. Sansa Stark was hidden away in the Vale by Petyr Baelish under a false name, while Arya Stark took ship for the free city of Braavos. Jon Snow, having repelled a wildling assault at the Wall, was chosen Lord Commander of the Night's Watch, with Stannis Baratheon encamped nearby. Daenerys Targaryen conquered the eastern slaver cities and settled to rule in Meereen. This volume follows the aftermath in the south and the west, while other threads unfold elsewhere at the same time.

characters.description: The witch at the center of Vampiric Charms. Rachel has survived several demon bargains and now knows that her childhood and Trent Kalamack's were linked by their fathers' genetic work. When Nick and Jax disappear in northern Michigan, she treats their rescue as a personal obligation despite Nick's abandonment of their relationship.
characters.name: Rachel Morgan

characters.description: Rachel's living-vampire partner and church housemate. Ivy remains affected by Piscary's old control and by Rachel's relationship with Kisten, but her loyalty makes it unlikely that she will remain behind once Rachel's rescue mission becomes more dangerous than planned.
characters.name: Ivy Tamwood

characters.description: The pixy partner in Vampiric Charms and Jax's father. Jenks has been estranged from Rachel over her secrecy, but news that his son is missing gives them an urgent reason to repair enough of their partnership to work together.
characters.name: Jenks

characters.description: Jenks's wife and the practical center of their large pixy family. Matalina understands why Jenks must search for Jax while also seeing the dangers in magic that changes a pixy's size and natural limits.
characters.name: Matalina

characters.description: Rachel's former boyfriend, a human researcher who left Cincinnati after being bound to her as a familiar. Nick is now missing after a theft involving Jax and a powerful Were artifact, and the limited information reaching Rachel casts him as a captive in need of rescue.
characters.name: Nick Sparagmos

characters.description: Jenks and Matalina's son, a young pixy determined to prove himself beyond his father's protection. Jax has been working with Nick and disappears with him after their attempt to obtain a valuable object draws the attention of hostile Weres.
characters.name: Jax

characters.description: The ancient elf living at the church after Rachel freed her from Algaliarept. Ceri combines knowledge of demon curses with caution learned through captivity, and she helps adapt dangerous magic for the unusual demands of Jenks's rescue mission.
characters.name: Ceridwen Merriam Dulciate

characters.description: A lone Were and insurance investigator who has worked with Rachel before. David needs pack standing without submitting to a conventional alpha and asks Rachel to take a formal place beside him, a bond with both social and magical consequences.
characters.name: David Hue

characters.description: A living vampire involved romantically with Rachel and tied by long history to Ivy. Kisten remains in Cincinnati during the initial search and provides a connection to the unstable vampire world the partners leave behind.
characters.name: Kisten Felps

characters.description: The secretive elven businessman whose past is entangled with Rachel's childhood. Trent has an interest in the object Nick and Jax pursued and sends his own people to protect his claim, making his agents another danger around the rescue.
characters.name: Trent Kalamack

characters.description: Trent's elven security chief. Quen follows the trail north on his employer's behalf and approaches Rachel as a capable rival whose objectives overlap with his only temporarily.
characters.name: Quen Hanson

recaps.ending: Rachel and her allies escape the northern Were factions with Nick and Jax alive. The immediate pack leaders pursuing them are defeated or driven off, but the Were Focus is not destroyed; Rachel brings the artifact back to Cincinnati, where its ability to unite Were packs makes possession of it a continuing political danger. She learns that Nick was not merely a victim. He helped steal the Focus from Trent and allowed Rachel to enter the conflict without telling her the truth, using her loyalty to improve his own chance of escape. Rachel ends their relationship decisively and no longer treats him as a trusted ally. Jenks returns safely to pixy size after the curse that let him travel and fight as a human-sized partner, though Jax's choices leave strain within the family. Rachel's pack bond with David remains in force. Ivy and Rachel survive the rescue with their partnership intact but their intimate and vampiric boundaries still unresolved. Trent does not recover the Focus, and the history Rachel shares with him yields no new trust.
recaps.in_short: When Nick and Jenks's son Jax disappear after stealing a potent Were artifact, Rachel and Jenks travel to northern Michigan to rescue them. Ceri uses demon-derived magic to make Jenks human-sized, letting him operate openly beyond pixy territory. Rachel also joins David Hue's small pack, gaining standing in Were society. They find Nick and Jax caught among rival Were factions seeking the Focus, an artifact capable of uniting packs under one leader. Ivy follows the rescue and helps them survive the escalating conflict, while Trent's agents pursue his claim to the stolen object. Rachel and her allies escape with both captives alive and the immediate pursuers defeated. The rescue also exposes Nick's betrayal: he participated willingly in the theft and withheld the truth so Rachel would help him. Rachel ends their relationship. Jenks returns to normal size, Rachel's pack bond with David continues, and she carries the Focus back to Cincinnati rather than resolving the larger struggle over it. The object leaves her vulnerable to every faction that wants to control the Weres.

recaps.text: Previously: Rachel Morgan founded Vampiric Charms with living vampire Ivy Tamwood and pixy Jenks after leaving Inderland Security. She exposed Trent Kalamack as secretly elven, then cleared him of a later series of witch murders by proving undead vampire master Piscary was the killer. Piscary was imprisoned, destabilizing Cincinnati's vampires. Rachel freed the ancient elf Ceri from demon Algaliarept but accumulated demon marks and obligations of her own. Nick Sparagmos, Rachel's human boyfriend and accidental familiar, left Cincinnati; Rachel began a relationship with living vampire Kisten. Trent later hired Rachel during a conflict with demon practitioner Lee Saladan. Rachel caused Al to take Lee as his familiar and learned that her father worked with Trent's father, that she and Trent knew one another as children, and that their families' genetic work was connected to curing her fatal Rosewood syndrome. Rachel starts this book separated from Nick, still tied to Al, and on strained terms with Jenks.

Rachel learns that Nick and Jax, Jenks's son, are missing in northern Michigan after becoming involved in the theft of a valuable object. Whatever Rachel's anger at Nick, she believes both captives will be killed without help. The crisis gives her and Jenks a reason to set aside the resentment caused by her secrecy. Because a pixy cannot simply travel and operate through human spaces like a full-sized partner, Ceri adapts dangerous transformation magic to make Jenks human-sized for the mission. The change gives him reach and physical power but carries unknown costs, and Matalina makes clear that returning him safely matters as much as finding Jax. Rachel and Jenks leave Cincinnati to follow the pair's trail.

On the road north, Rachel and human-sized Jenks adjust to working together without his usual ability to vanish into gardens and airspace. Jenks's combat skills and senses remain valuable, but his altered body makes him visible and changes the balance between them. Their search establishes that Nick and Jax were pursuing an artifact known as the Focus and that several Were groups now want it. David Hue helps Rachel understand the pack rules surrounding the conflict. Rachel formally joins a pack with him, giving David the standing he needs and giving Rachel a recognized position among Weres, though the bond entails obligations neither can treat as a convenient disguise.

Rachel and Jenks reach the Mackinaw area and begin locating the factions holding Nick and Jax. The Focus is more than stolen property: it can concentrate Were allegiance and potentially place many packs under one leader. That power explains why negotiation repeatedly gives way to capture and violence. Trent Kalamack also has a claim connected to the object and sends Quen north, adding an elven recovery effort whose goals only partly overlap with Rachel's rescue. Rachel avoids giving either the Weres or Trent's people full knowledge of her plans. The evidence still presents Nick and Jax primarily as prisoners caught after a reckless theft, so Rachel concentrates on reaching them before deciding who should possess the artifact.

The rescue becomes a moving contest among rival Were factions, Rachel's group, and Trent's agents. Rachel uses her new pack status with David and magic Ceri helped prepare, while Jenks takes advantage of the strength and reach of his temporary body. Ivy follows from Cincinnati and joins the struggle, unwilling to leave Rachel inside a conflict that now includes captivity, pack dominance, and supernatural coercion. Her arrival gives Rachel a powerful ally but also brings their unresolved issues of blood and trust into close quarters. Rachel reaches Nick and Jax, yet gaps in Nick's account suggest that the theft and his role in it are not as simple as the plea for rescue implied.

Rachel's group tries to move Nick, Jax, and the Focus out of the Mackinaw conflict while the Were factions close in. Control of the artifact could reshape pack society, so surrendering it to the nearest claimant would not create a neutral outcome. Quen's priority is recovering Trent's property and preserving elven interests; Rachel's is keeping her people alive and preventing one faction from using the Focus immediately. Nick's decisions before his capture become increasingly suspect, straining any hope that rescue will restore their former relationship. Jenks must also protect Jax while confronting the possibility that his son chose the risk rather than merely following Nick. None of those conflicts can be settled until the group survives the final pursuit.

Rachel, Ivy, Jenks, and their allies defeat or escape the immediate Were leaders pursuing them and get Nick and Jax out alive. Rachel retains the Focus and carries it back to Cincinnati instead of giving the artifact to a faction that could use it to dominate the packs; its continued existence means the larger political struggle is postponed rather than ended. Nick is exposed as a willing participant in the theft who concealed the truth and counted on Rachel's loyalty to rescue him. Rachel ends their romantic and working relationship. Jenks is restored to pixy size after the human-sized curse, while Jax's independence and deception leave a family breach that rescue alone cannot repair. Rachel's pack bond with David remains valid. Ivy returns with Rachel, their loyalty proven again even though the blood and intimacy at the center of their relationship remain unresolved. Trent loses the immediate recovery contest but retains his knowledge of Rachel and their shared past.

characters.description: A university professor, Red Guard consultant, and Sebastien's mentor. He studies the Raven Queen while negotiating access to a protected archaeological project, approaching both investigations as routes to otherwise restricted knowledge.
characters.name: Thaddeus Lacer

characters.description: A university history-department grandmaster who summons Thaddeus Lacer, questions him about the Raven Queen investigation, and controls access to protected archaeological material. The grandmaster offers information in exchange for Lacer's cooperation and secrecy.
characters.name: History-department grandmaster

characters.description: A gifted university thaumaturge and Thaddeus Lacer's apprentice. During a defensive practical, Sebastien becomes the group's strategist, combining adaptable spellwork with a strong preference for keeping teammates alive.
characters.name: Sebastien Siverling

characters.description: Sebastien's trusted classmate and defensive-magic teammate. Damien contributes scouting and camouflage tools while following Sebastien's tactical lead.
characters.name: Damien Westbay

characters.description: A member of the Gervin family and one of Sebastien's allies. Anna responds to the defensive-practical alarm by helping contain damaging gossip and offering practical social support.
characters.name: Anna Gervin

characters.description: Anna's younger sister and another ally of Sebastien. Natalia joins Anna in planning a response to rumors after the university mistakes Sebastien's unusual conduit technique for dangerous magic, helping protect Sebastien's standing among the students.
characters.name: Natalia Gervin

characters.description: A covert contact who passes along Thaddeus Lacer's request for a meeting with the Raven Queen. Oliver protects Sebastien's invented history while pursuing interests of his own, leaving her dependent on assistance whose full purpose she cannot safely assume.
characters.name: Oliver Dryden

characters.description: An independent thaumaturge whom Oliver regards as trustworthy but not necessarily honorable. Sebastien considers Liza a possible custodian for sensitive property, yet remains unwilling to rely on her completely.
characters.name: Liza

characters.description: Damien's brother and the Lord Commander of the Coppers. Titus investigates Sebastien's background, her connection to Damien, and her association with Oliver, making him an official obstacle to her secrecy.
characters.name: Titus Westbay

characters.description: Siobhan is Sebastien Siverling beneath a set of magical disguises and public identities. She uses these presentations to conduct covert work, negotiate through intermediaries, and keep the wanted Raven Queen separate from her university life.
characters.name: Siobhan

characters.description: A prognose woman attached to Lord Linwood's household and Millennium's mother. She agrees to deliver a covert letter and create a public distraction in exchange for a future spell meant to let her son sleep safely.
characters.name: Gera

characters.description: Head of the Linwood household and an affiliate of the Nightmare Pack. His home shelters Gera and Millennium and provides Siobhan with a discreet place to arrange services, communicate with trusted intermediaries, and appear as the Raven Queen.
characters.name: Lord Linwood

characters.description: Gera's fae-blooded son, troubled by predictive visions that disrupt his sleep. Millennium meets Siobhan at Lord Linwood's home, where she offers practical comfort while owing his mother a more durable solution.
characters.name: Millennium Linwood

characters.description: Sebastien's imprisoned father. Sebastien expects his approaching sentencing to give the Coppers an occasion to renew their attempt to locate the Raven Queen.
characters.name: Ennis Nott

characters.description: A university contact whom Sebastien approaches for a discreet meeting, expecting Tanya to recognize an unsigned request without attracting attention.
characters.name: Tanya Canelo

characters.description: A severely malnourished orphan whom Sebastien finds ill after eating unsafe food. Sebastien brings Betty to a healer and persuades the Lord Commander to pay for her treatment, overnight care, and short-term aid.
characters.name: Betty

characters.description: Millennium Linwood’s maid, who accompanies him and his protectors while they flee Pendragon operatives.
characters.name: Martha

characters.description: Katerine's nephew and one of the children held with Millennium in a sensory-deprivation prison. Theo is injured but alive when Siobhan finds the captives and begins organizing their escape from guards who are prepared to use lethal force.
characters.name: Theo

characters.description: A Verdant Stag enforcer imprisoned with the abducted civilians. Though badly beaten, Gerard remains able to organize the other captives as Siobhan works to free them, providing order while injuries and renewed attacks threaten the group.
characters.name: Enforcer Gerard

characters.description: A Verdant Stag enforcer gravely injured during the abduction. Turner has a serious broken leg when Siobhan finds him among the captives.
characters.name: Enforcer Turner

characters.description: A Pendragon operative who abandons his former side during the escape. Anders accepts a bargain with Siobhan in exchange for healing and extending the life of his disabled dog, then helps the captives evade the organization he previously served.
characters.name: Anders

characters.description: A defecting Pendragon operative who helps conceal the escape group. Parker worries that association with Siobhan will endanger his daughter and aunt, and seeks protection for them in exchange for further service.
characters.name: Parker

characters.description: A senior Verdant Stag operator and aunt of one of the rescued children. Katerine arrives at the warded arena after learning that the children are safe.
characters.name: Katerine

characters.description: A burned survivor of the abduction and an outspoken follower of the Raven Queen. Deidre plans to collect accounts from the rescued captives, helping turn their incomplete observations into a shared legend.
characters.name: Deidre Johnson

characters.description: Anders’s elderly, gravely injured dog. Siobhan has promised to restore Bear’s health and grant him an exceptionally long life.
characters.name: Bear

characters.description: A Pendragon operative who survives Siobhan's shadow creature entering his body. Healers cannot determine its continuing effect on Jorgensen.
characters.name: Jorgensen

characters.description: Siobhan's short-lived persona for gaining access to Willowdale alongside Liza. The disguise casts her as Liza's relative from Silva Erde and an apprentice healer.
characters.name: Amelia

characters.description: A surviving archaeologist from the Black Wastes expedition. Edgar is paranoid, prone to hallucinations, and detached from his own name, but remains a possible witness to what was recovered from Merton's hermitage.
characters.name: Edgar

characters.description: A university grandmaster connected to the Architects of Khronos. Kiernan seeks Merton's alleged process for converting magical beast cores into usable solarium.
characters.name: Grandmaster Kiernan

characters.description: Anastasia Gervin is Sebastien's ally Anna Gervin. She openly supports and protects Sebastien during a difficult meeting with Oliver Dryden.
characters.name: Anastasia Gervin

characters.description: An unidentified Red Guard operative who confines Siobhan in a distorted space and imposes a three-minute contest with lethal terms. The agent wields a parasitic aberrant flesh glove that can sever physical matter and magical connections.
characters.name: Masked Red Guard agent

recaps.ending: Sebastien survives the High Crown's hostage operation and a Red Guard contest, but both conflicts leave lasting exposure. She keeps her identities separate from the public, acquires a private home and warded resources, opens Merton's journal, and gains the effective raven sleep proxy. Thaddeus Lacer returns her mother's genuine ring and agrees to represent her interests within the Red Guard, while remaining unaware that the being sealed in her memory briefly controlled her detached shadow. Oliver retains a different journal, and their damaged partnership resumes on guarded, more equal terms. Damien continues investigating suppressed Red Guard conduct without knowing Sebastien is the Raven Queen. Liza, Anna, the Nightmare Pack, and the Verdant Stag survivors remain allies with separate obligations. Ennis is free but missing, Edgar has vanished, Parker is dead, and Parker's family has been relocated. Kiernan has stopped answering while an Architects of Khronos team threatens people in Osham. The solarium shortage, the missing fifth journal, the sealed being, Red Guard attention, and the Raven Queen's expanding organized worship all remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Sebastien begins the term under official scrutiny while preparing to break the sympathetic link authorities can use against the Raven Queen. A High Crown operation instead abducts her with children and faction allies, hoping the captives will draw the Raven Queen into a trap. She escapes sensory deprivation, turns two guards, rescues the prisoners, and leads them out, though Parker is captured and later dies. While recovering, she learns that five Merton journals may exist and that one may describe converting beast cores into solarium as natural supplies fail. Oliver admits stealing that journal, fracturing their alliance, while Sebastien eventually opens her own. Her sleep-proxy research succeeds, Ennis escapes, and Damien joins a cautious investigation into Red Guard abuses. A Red Guard contest ends when the being sealed in Sebastien's memory takes control of her detached shadow. Thaddeus Lacer becomes her tentative intermediary and returns her mother's ring. She and Oliver restore limited cooperation, but the Architects' Osham operation and an uncontrolled faith in the Raven Queen remain open.

recaps.text: Previously: Sebastien Siverling established herself as a gifted university thaumaturge while concealing dangerous private work behind several identities. She studies under Thaddeus Lacer and relies on Damien Westbay as a friend and classmate, though Damien does not know the full nature of her secrets. Oliver Dryden protects her invented background and serves as a covert ally, but his political interests make complete trust impossible. Liza works with Sebastien on difficult magical research under similarly guarded terms. Tanya Canelo is entangled with the Architects of Khronos, while Sebastien's father, Ennis Nott, remains imprisoned. Beyond the university, the wanted Raven Queen has become important to the Verdant Stag and Nightmare Pack and remains the target of persistent official investigations. Sebastien also possesses an inaccessible journal recovered from Merton's hermitage. Its changing glyphs have resisted ordinary attempts to read it, leaving both its contents and its connection to wider conflicts unknown.

Thaddeus Lacer joins a protected university effort to unlock archaeological material while seeking contact with the Raven Queen. At the university, Sebastien leads a defensive practical across a simulated city. When she casts through Damien's conduit against her calf, faculty mistake the technique for flesh-casting and halt the examination. Lacer verifies that the difficult method is legitimate, clearing her of an imminent aberrance event. Sebastien then earns exceptional recognition for a complex exhibition and is formally accepted as Lacer's apprentice, though he identifies a weakness in her darkness-focused transmogrification. Official attention remains a separate danger. An investigator questions Damien about Sebastien's connection to Oliver, and Sebastien preserves her cover by supporting Damien's mistaken theory about a secret organization. She asks Damien to compare decades of rogue-magic and Red Guard records for suspicious discrepancies. She also decides to seek a surviving member of the Black Wastes expedition at Willowdale, hoping for a new path toward understanding the journal recovered from Merton's hermitage.

Sebastien fails to decrypt the hidden journal and grows more suspicious of Oliver, whose fabricated history for her has attracted Titus Westbay's investigation. Oliver says the cover still holds, but its invented past needs reinforcement. Sebastien chooses to meet Titus directly rather than wait for him to uncover inconsistencies. Under her alternate identities, she also arranges a letter to the High Crown and bargains with Gera for delivery and a future public distraction, promising a sleep-transfer spell for Millennium in return. With Liza, she begins human trials of a raven-based sleep proxy and plans to destroy the blood sample used by the Coppers to locate the Raven Queen. The operation is meant to coincide with Ennis Nott's sentencing. Sebastien's first-term results are strong, and Lacer helps her select and translate a demanding restorative spell. Her attempt at negotiation fails when the High Crown publicly promises the Raven Queen's capture and execution. Still needing money and assistance, Sebastien develops a selective darkness product, approaches Tanya Canelo for covert work, and begins her meeting with Titus while keeping her larger plan concealed.

Titus acknowledges that he overread the evidence around Sebastien after she pushes him to help a starving orphan, though she intends to avoid him afterward. Sebastien restricts her own access to a substance she fears she depends on, then recruits Tanya to impersonate the Raven Queen from a distance during the sentencing operation. Lacer's work reveals that the protected journals respond to identity and sequences of concepts rather than ordinary ciphers. Sebastien discovers that she can maintain two separate magical wills, passes the journal's two-concept test, and names her counter-scrying plan Operation Palimpsest. She also learns a restorative light technique and locates the recovering expedition survivor at Willowdale, where Liza has an unexplained treatment role. On the sentencing day, Tanya arrives injured after an Architects of Khronos mission lost a dangerous shipment to a military team. Siobhan heals her and proceeds with the plan, but suspects the Coppers have placed a broad compulsion over the city to draw in the Raven Queen. Before she reaches Liza's protection, a Copper stops her in the street.

Millennium helps Siobhan escape the Copper's scrutiny, but Pendragon operatives use him as bait and capture their group with a stun trap. The kidnappers take Siobhan, Millennium, Theo, and members of the Nightmare Pack and Verdant Stag to an underground prison under complete sensory deprivation. Siobhan uses her active will to regain limited awareness, adapts her shadow familiar into a substitute sense, and escapes the deprivation array. Meanwhile, the planned mass of ravens draws the official force away from Ennis's sentencing. Inside the complex, Siobhan frees the other captives but is badly injured by a radiant explosive and confined in a bright cell. Recognizing that concussion and will strain are impairing her judgment, she abandons a reckless escape attempt. Instead, she frightens two guards into bargaining. They agree to neutralize their loyalty vows and help her in exchange for personal boons. The defectors release the prisoners, recover their equipment, and destroy stored blood and hair that could be used for tracking. With reinforcements approaching, Siobhan covers the group in darkness and leads them into an uncertain tunnel route.

Siobhan repairs Enforcer Turner's shattered leg well enough for travel and extends her anti-divination shadow over the fugitives. Anders and Parker, the two defectors, guide the group toward a gulf ferry station. They steal a boat and disable a pursuing vessel, but Parker is harpooned and pulled into Pendragon custody. Thaddeus secretly helps the remaining escapees by killing two pursuers and damaging their boat while concealing his intervention from the authorities. The survivors reach a warded arena, where Liza confirms that the planned operation destroyed the Coppers' usable blood sample. Siobhan is left with serious injuries and will strain. The rescued factions arrange protection while Katerine and Gera treat the kidnapping as an act of war against their families. Siobhan refuses immediate retaliation but asks them to protect the survivors and help honor the boons she promised. Deidre Johnson begins gathering accounts that strengthen the Raven Queen's supernatural reputation. At court, the High Crown confirms that the children were taken to pressure allied factions and lure the Raven Queen. Thaddeus realizes Sebastien was also an intended hostage, while the shadow's unexplained effect on Jorgensen deepens official fear.

While recovering, Siobhan accepts that an unknown presence is sealed within her mind and contacts Thaddeus for information about consciousness held inside memory. Parker is tortured in Crown custody and later dies, leaving Siobhan determined to protect his family. The other abductees and their relatives are successfully hidden or relocated. At Willowdale, Siobhan meets Edgar, the recovering Black Wastes archaeologist. He says the expedition found five Merton journals rather than four and believes a missing volume could be important enough to cause conflict with Osham. Sebastien begins a ritual intended to create an untraceable guiding symbol, but fears its language may be influenced by the sealed presence. She gives Damien a limited account of the abduction, and he accepts that the High Crown committed atrocities while continuing their records research. The new university term begins with Tanya serving as Lacer's student aide. Lacer explains that transmogrification depends on shared cultural associations, revealing why Sebastien's literal thinking has impaired her casting. She learns how to work with that principle, but also discovers that the Red Guard has opened an investigation into whether the Raven Queen poses an exceptional threat.

Sebastien masters output detachment and improves her troubled transmogrification, then confronts Grandmaster Kiernan. He says the Architects of Khronos seek a journal describing how to convert beast cores into solarium because the mines may fail within a decade. Edgar's report of a fifth journal changes the search. Oliver then admits that he arranged the theft of one Merton journal, while Sebastien reveals that she holds another. She accuses him of benefiting from her stolen-book crisis, and their friendship collapses into a pact of mutual secrecy. Sebastien builds independent housing, communications, identities, and warded storage. The Nightmare Pack relocates vulnerable survivors and Parker's family, while Siobhan and Liza use nonlethal vitality transfers to greatly improve Anders's dying dog. Anna confirms that she independently forged her father's signature to block Oliver's contract. Sebastien tells Lacer that she is Siobhan and the Raven Queen and can split her will. Damien commits to cautious research into suspected Red Guard abuses. Liza's raven sleep proxy succeeds, giving Siobhan sustained rest, and Ennis escapes his labor camp. Kiernan and Lacer offer conditional journal cooperation. At last, Sebastien passes the final glyph test and opens her previously unreadable journal.

Merton's journal proves difficult to read even after opening, though it records self-charging artifacts and related lost techniques. The Architects stage a false Raven Queen sighting in Silva Erde, then Tanya warns that one of their teams plans to abduct people in Osham. Oliver tries to contact Kiernan, but no reply arrives. During a renewed sleep-proxy period, a masked Red Guard agent traps Siobhan in a space distorted by supernatural rain and offers a lethal timed contest. The agent's aberrant flesh glove cuts both matter and magical connections, and hidden binding magic turns Siobhan's attacks into worsening cold backlash. When her detached shadow becomes autonomous, the being sealed in her memory uses it to confront the Red Guard and force her escape. The being then withdraws, leaving Siobhan aware that added power and separation from the seal can give it an opening. She seeks help from Thaddeus. He returns her mother's genuine solarium ring, admits replacing it with a dangerous flawed ring, and agrees to serve as her Red Guard intermediary. At Theo's birthday, Sebastien and Oliver restore a guarded alliance based on mutual secrets. Kiernan and the Osham targets remain missing from contact, while organized worship of the Raven Queen spreads beyond Siobhan's control.

characters.description: Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North, ruler of the vast northern half of the Seven Kingdoms. Stern, plainspoken, and devoted to duty, family, and the old gods of his homeland. Years earlier he helped his friend Robert Baratheon win the throne in rebellion, and he still keeps to the harder, more honest customs of the North. Married to Catelyn Tully, he is father to five trueborn children and guardian of a baseborn son. He prizes honor above ambition and is deeply uneasy with the flattery and scheming of the southern court.
characters.name: Eddard Stark

characters.description: Lady of Winterfell, born to House Tully of Riverrun in the south and wed to Eddard Stark. A strong-willed, capable, and protective mother who keeps the worship of the Seven rather than her husband's old gods. Warm toward her own children but cold toward her husband's bastard, whose presence she has never forgiven. Politically shrewd, she is fiercely loyal to her family and its interests.
characters.name: Catelyn Stark

characters.description: The eldest trueborn son of Eddard and Catelyn Stark and heir to Winterfell. A dutiful, well-trained youth in his mid-teens who carries himself with the seriousness of a boy raised to one day rule the North.
characters.name: Robb Stark

characters.description: Eddard Stark's bastard son, raised at Winterfell beside the trueborn children but always set a little apart by his birth. Close in age and friendship to Robb, quiet and skilled with a blade, he knows a bastard can inherit nothing. He is drawn toward the Night's Watch, the sworn brotherhood that mans the great Wall guarding the realm's far north.
characters.name: Jon Snow

characters.description: The elder Stark daughter, a graceful and courteous girl devoted to songs, courtesy, and the ideals of southern chivalry. She dreams of marrying a gallant highborn prince and becoming a great lady of the court.
characters.name: Sansa Stark

characters.description: The younger Stark daughter, a willful, restless tomboy who prefers riding, adventure, and swordplay to needlework and ladylike manners, and who is often at odds with her prim elder sister.
characters.name: Arya Stark

characters.description: The second Stark son, a boy of seven who loves to scale the walls and towers of Winterfell and dreams of one day growing up to be a knight.
characters.name: Bran Stark

characters.description: King of the Seven Kingdoms, who seized the crown in a rebellion years before with Eddard Stark at his side. Once a mighty warrior and Ned's closest friend, he has grown fat, restless, and weary of the labor of ruling, far fonder of feasting, hunting, and drink than of governance. He is wed, unhappily, to Cersei of House Lannister.
characters.name: Robert Baratheon

characters.description: Queen to King Robert and a proud, beautiful daughter of the immensely wealthy House Lannister of Casterly Rock. Ambitious and watchful, she guards her family's power and her own standing at court with cold intelligence.
characters.name: Cersei Lannister

characters.description: Cersei's dazzling twin brother, a gifted and handsome knight of the Kingsguard. He is known as the Kingslayer for having slain the previous king, the very man he had sworn to protect, during the rebellion that put Robert on the throne, a deed that stains his golden reputation.
characters.name: Jaime Lannister

characters.description: The youngest of the Lannister siblings, a dwarf mocked as the Imp and little loved by his own family. Denied a warrior's stature, he arms himself instead with a sharp tongue, wide reading, and a keen understanding of people, and takes his pleasures in wine and clever talk. He is the cleverest Lannister and the least respected.
characters.name: Tyrion Lannister

characters.description: A young princess of the fallen House Targaryen, the dynasty that once ruled the Seven Kingdoms astride dragons until Robert's rebellion cast it down. Exiled across the narrow sea since infancy, she has lived in poverty and fear under her domineering elder brother Viserys, who clings to the dream of reclaiming the throne. Timid at the outset, she is sold in marriage to a powerful warlord of the nomadic Dothraki to buy her brother an army.
characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen

recaps.ending: Ned Stark is executed on King Joffrey's order despite the mercy he was promised, shattering any hope of peace. His son Robb, declared King in the North, wins his early battles and captures the knight Jaime Lannister, with his mother Catelyn at his side. Sansa remains a captive in King's Landing, betrothed to the boy king who killed her father, while Arya, disguised as a boy, escapes the capital and is carried northward. Crippled Bran and his little brother Rickon remain at Winterfell, and Bran is troubled by vivid wolf-dreams. Jon Snow commits fully to the Night's Watch as unmistakable signs mount that the ancient enemy beyond the Wall is returning. Farthest away, Daenerys Targaryen, widowed and childless after the death of Khal Drogo, steps into his funeral pyre clutching three fossilized dragon eggs and rises from the ashes unburned, three living dragons clinging to her, reborn as a queen with a power the world had thought long dead. The realm has broken into open war, and every side believes itself the rightful one.
recaps.in_short: Lord Eddard Stark leaves Winterfell to serve his friend King Robert as Hand of the King, a post whose previous holder was murdered. Investigating in the capital, Ned learns the deadly secret that Queen Cersei's children are not the king's but were fathered by her own twin brother, Jaime Lannister. Before he can act, Robert dies of a hunting wound, and Cersei's cruel son Joffrey takes the throne. Betrayed by allies he trusted, Ned is arrested and, despite a promise of mercy, publicly beheaded. His son Robb raises the North and is proclaimed King in the North, while Robert's brothers Stannis and Renly each claim the crown too, plunging the realm into war. The Stark family is scattered: Sansa a hostage, Arya fleeing in disguise, Bran crippled and left at Winterfell, and Jon Snow sworn to the Night's Watch as an ancient enemy wakes beyond the Wall. Across the sea, the exiled Daenerys Targaryen loses her warlord husband and unborn child, then walks into his funeral pyre and emerges unburned with three newborn dragons, the first the world has seen in over a century.

recaps.text: The story opens in the North of a land called the Seven Kingdoms, where seasons last for years and a long winter is feared to be coming. Lord Eddard Stark rules the ancient castle of Winterfell as Warden of the North. Far to the north, beyond a colossal ice Wall manned by the sworn brothers of the Night's Watch, something old and cold is beginning to stir in the haunted forest. When the king's chief minister, the Hand of the King, dies unexpectedly, King Robert Baratheon travels north to Winterfell to ask his old friend and comrade Ned to take the dead man's place at court. The Stark children come into possession of a litter of direwolf pups, the sigil of their house. Far across the sea, the last exiled children of the overthrown dragon dynasty scheme to win back the throne their family lost. It is a realm of great houses, old grudges, and looming winter, where a game of thrones is quietly beginning.

characters.description: One of the last Antari, the Red London crown's messenger, and the adopted brother of its heir. Months after the trouble with the black stone he is watched, restricted and blamed: his travelling has been curtailed, the king no longer trusts him with much, and the bond he made to save Rhy means every risk he takes is also someone else's. Restless and increasingly reckless about it, he looks for somewhere to put the part of himself that is not allowed out any more.
characters.name: Kell

characters.description: The Grey London thief who talked her way into a world with magic and then onto a ship. She now sails with a privateer crew, learning the trade and the sea, and hiding how fast her own magic is growing and what her missing eye conceals. She is a quick study, an enthusiastic fighter, and entirely uninterested in going back to being anyone's passenger.
characters.name: Delilah Bard

characters.description: Captain of the Night Spire, a privateer sailing under the Arnesian crown's licence to rob its enemies. Born into a Red London noble house and no longer welcome in it, he is charming, vain, generous with his crew and very good at his work. He sees magic as colored threads around a person, which is how he notices what Lila is trying to keep to herself.
characters.name: Alucard Emery

characters.description: The heir to Red London's throne, who survived what happened to him only because Kell tied their lives together. He cannot die while Kell lives, and he feels everything Kell feels. He has thrown himself into staging a great international magicians' tournament in his city, partly out of genuine ambition and partly to outrun what was done to him.
characters.name: Rhy Maresh

characters.description: The White London Antari, who was pushed through a sealed door into a dead world with a fragment of its magic bound inside him, and who did not die there. Broken, starving and alone in the ruins of Black London, he is found by something that offers to make him whole and to give him back his own ruined city, in exchange for a great deal more than he is being told.
characters.name: Holland

characters.description: The living magic of Black London: a will with no body, ancient and enormously powerful, that speaks in offers and bargains. It is patient, persuasive, and keeps its promises only in the letter. What it wants is what it has always wanted, a world to remake and a body strong enough to carry it into one.
characters.name: Osaron

characters.description: A White London fighter with yellow eyes, raised up out of the city's gutters into something far stronger than she was born as, and loyal to the man who did it. She is sent out of her world to do work that cannot be done openly.
characters.name: Ojka

characters.description: The head priest of the London Sanctuary, who reads the balance of a person's magic at a glance and has known Kell since he was a child. He is one of the few people in the city who treats both Kell and Rhy as people rather than as instruments of the crown.
characters.name: Tieren Serense

characters.description: The king of Red London, who now regards Kell less as a second son than as a danger to be managed, and who has drawn the leash in accordingly.
characters.name: King Maxim Maresh

characters.description: The queen of Red London and Rhy's mother, whose fondness for Kell has cooled into something closer to fear since her son nearly died.
characters.name: Queen Emira Maresh

characters.description: A young royal guard assigned to the prince, good-natured and devout, who takes Rhy's safety a good deal more personally than the posting requires.
characters.name: Hastra

characters.description: The elder of the two Veskan royals sent to Red London for the tournament: large, physical, openly competitive, and pleased to be somewhere he can prove it.
characters.name: Prince Col

characters.description: The younger Veskan royal, small, cheerful and considerably sharper than the people around her assume. She is very interested in the Arnesian prince, and asks him a great many friendly questions.
characters.name: Princess Cora

characters.description: One of the celebrated Arnesian competitors in the tournament and a favorite of the crowds, with a considerable following in the city before the first match is fought.
characters.name: Kisimyr Vasrin

characters.description: A Veskan competitor in the tournament, a wind magician with a light, showy style that makes him popular with spectators.
characters.name: Jinnar

recaps.ending: The tournament ends in disaster instead of a ceremony. Ojka lures Kell away from the arena and very nearly kills him before Lila reaches them and kills her instead. Holland then takes Kell himself and drags him through to White London, because what Osaron needs is an Antari, and Kell's blood will open a door into a living world. In the palace, Rhy is stabbed in the chaos and does not die, because he cannot while Kell lives, and the carefully kept secret of what Kell did to save him is no longer safe. Lila's own nature is now known to Kell and Alucard: she is Antari, the third of them, self-taught and largely untrained. She forces Alucard to turn the Night Spire toward White London to go after Kell. The book closes with Kell a prisoner in the world he was warned about, Rhy wounded on a throne he has not inherited, Holland restored and no longer anyone's servant, and Osaron poised to cross into a living city.
recaps.in_short: Four months after the black stone, Kell is a restricted, resented royal messenger and Rhy, unkillable while Kell lives, is staging a great international magicians' tournament in Red London. Lila Bard has joined the privateer crew of Captain Alucard Emery, learning the sea and hiding how fast her magic is growing. In Black London, Holland is found half-dead by Osaron, the living magic of that dead world, and takes its bargain: it makes him whole, restores White London to life, and puts him on its throne, in exchange for a way into a living world. Holland sends his agent Ojka after Kell. In Red London, Kell enters the tournament in disguise and so does Lila, and their secrets come apart in front of each other: Lila is Antari too. The tournament is broken up by an attack. Lila kills Ojka, but Holland takes Kell through to White London to use his blood as a doorway, and Rhy is stabbed and survives only because of the bond. Lila and Alucard sail for White London.

recaps.text: Previously: four Londons occupy the same point in different worlds, and only Antari, marked by one solid black eye, can travel between them. Kell, raised in the Red London palace as the crown's messenger, was handed a black stone that turned out to be a piece of Black London, the world magic consumed and which was sealed away centuries ago. Hunted for it, he was robbed of it in Grey London by a street thief named Delilah Bard, and the two of them ended up carrying it back toward its source together. The rulers of White London, the twins Athos and Astrid Dane, wanted the stone for their starving world; they kept the only other living Antari, Holland, bound to their service by a spell cut into his skin. Lila killed Athos and Kell broke Holland's binding, but Astrid had already crossed into Red London and taken Prince Rhy's body. Kell destroyed her, which meant killing his brother, then tied his own life to Rhy's with Antari blood magic to bring him back. Rhy now cannot die while Kell lives, and the two of them share pain. Kell bound the stone into the dying Holland, pushed him through the door into Black London and sealed it. Lila, refusing a comfortable place in a magical world, left for a ship of her own.

Four months on, Lila Bard is at sea. She has talked her way onto the Night Spire, a privateer ship licensed by the Arnesian crown, whose captain, Alucard Emery, is an exiled Red London noble with an eye for magic and for people who are hiding something. She is learning the trade, learning to fight, and quietly teaching herself magic. In Red London, Kell is under a much shorter leash: the king has curtailed his travelling, the court blames him for what nearly happened to the prince, and the bond he made means anything he suffers Rhy suffers too. Rhy, unable to die and unable to say so, is throwing himself into organizing a great international magicians' tournament to be hosted by his city. And in the dead world beyond the sealed door, Holland is not dead. Starving among the ruins of Black London, he is found by something that speaks to him and offers him a bargain.

The thing that found Holland is Osaron, the living magic of Black London: a will without a body, ancient and patient, that trades in offers. It makes Holland whole again and gives him what he has wanted his whole life, his own city restored, and in return it means to be carried into a living world. Holland returns to White London, takes its throne, and watches the grey city come back to life around him. He raises up a fighter named Ojka, giving her strength she was never born with, and sends her out to find Kell, because what Osaron needs is Antari blood. Meanwhile the Night Spire makes for Red London: Alucard has business there and the tournament is drawing competitors and royal delegations from Faro and Vesk. Lila, who has never been near a magical contest in her life, decides she is going to enter it.

The city fills up for the tournament. Kell, forbidden to compete as himself and desperate for anything that is his own, enters under a false name and a mask, with Rhy's collusion. Lila does the same, buying her way into another competitor's place. Alucard's arrival reopens old ground with Rhy, whom he knew well before he was exiled from the country, and puts him at odds with Kell immediately. Lila and Kell find each other again in the middle of it, both lying about what they are doing there. Alucard, who sees magic as threads of color, has already worked out that Lila is far more than a clever thief with a knife, and presses her about it.

The tournament runs through its rounds in front of the visiting courts, with Kell and Lila both advancing behind their disguises and neither able to say so aloud. In the process Lila's secret comes apart: she is Antari, the third living one, self-taught and largely untrained, and Kell and Alucard both learn it. Kell, who has spent the book being told what he is not allowed to be, has to decide what to do about a second unregistered Antari in a city that already fears the one it has. In White London, Holland's preparations are finished and Ojka has found what she was sent for; the attack on Red London is no longer a question of whether but of when, and it will come while the whole city is watching the arena.

The tournament ends in disaster rather than a ceremony. Ojka draws Kell away from the crowds and nearly kills him; Lila reaches them and kills her. It is not enough, because Ojka was only the opening move. Holland comes for Kell himself, overpowers him and drags him through to White London, since Osaron needs an Antari and Kell's blood will open a door into a living world. Inside the palace, Rhy is stabbed during the confusion and does not die, because he cannot while Kell lives; the secret of the bond, which the crown has guarded for months, is out. Lila, no longer hiding what she is, makes Alucard turn the Night Spire toward White London. The book closes with Kell a prisoner, Rhy wounded and effectively alone at the head of a frightened court, Holland restored and serving no one but the thing he bargained with, and Osaron ready to cross.

characters.description: The young witch of the Chalk, now eleven, leaving her downland home for the mountains to begin her formal training as an apprentice witch. Practical, strong-willed, and quietly proud of her growing ability, she carries a deep sense of responsibility for her home ground, along with an inexperience that leaves her vulnerable to temptations she does not yet recognize.
characters.name: Tiffany Aching

characters.description: The Big Man, or leader, of the Nac Mac Feegle, the fierce little blue-skinned Wee Free Men who regard Tiffany as their hag and protector. Loyal to the point of recklessness, he leads his clan to follow Tiffany into the mountains to keep her safe, even as changes in his own life among the Feegle weigh on him.
characters.name: Rob Anybody

characters.description: The traveling witch-finder who first recognized Tiffany's talent and who arranges her apprenticeship in the mountains. Bookish, brisk, and practical, she keeps a distant, watchful eye on her charge's progress.
characters.name: Miss Tick

characters.description: The new kelda, or queen, of Rob Anybody's Nac Mac Feegle clan, and his wife. Small, sharp, and formidable, she rules the mound with quiet authority and sees further and more clearly than the clan's rowdy warriors, sensing danger before it arrives.
characters.name: Jeannie

characters.description: The research witch to whom Tiffany is apprenticed, a kindly, unglamorous woman who lives and works in one body but is in fact a single mind occupying two bodies at once. She serves her scattered rural neighbours with steady, practical care, teaching Tiffany that witchcraft is mostly hard, humble work done for other people.
characters.name: Miss Level

characters.description: A domineering, self-important young witch apprentice who leads the local circle of trainee witches. Preoccupied with the image, jargon, and trappings of witchcraft, she looks down on plain country practice and treats Tiffany with lofty condescension.
characters.name: Annagramma

characters.description: A shy, kind-hearted young witch apprentice who specializes in the care of pigs. Unassuming and easily flustered, she becomes a genuine friend to Tiffany among the circle of trainees.
characters.name: Petulia

characters.description: An ancient, mindless, bodiless thing that has drifted through the world since the beginning of time, without self, thought, or purpose of its own. It is drawn irresistibly to the most powerful minds it can find, and seeks to possess them in order to feel, briefly, what it is to be alive. Tiffany's growing power makes her its target.
characters.name: The Hiver

characters.description: The most respected and formidable witch of the mountains, austere, sharp-eyed, and sparing with praise. She watches over Tiffany from a distance and understands, better than anyone, both the danger the girl is in and the strength she will need to find within herself to survive it.
characters.name: Granny Weatherwax

recaps.ending: Possessed by the hiver, Tiffany is turned into a proud, careless, and increasingly dangerous version of herself, the ancient thing riding her power without understanding it. The Feegle and Granny Weatherwax intervene, and with their help Tiffany claws her way back to awareness inside her own mind. She realizes that the hiver cannot be simply driven off or destroyed, because it has no self to attack: it is a formless thing that has never known what it is. Rather than fight it, she draws it fully into herself and then gives it the one thing it has always lacked, a sense of being someone who can die. Made aware of itself and of its own ending for the first time, the hiver is led gently to Death and finds the peace it never knew it wanted. This happens around the great gathering the witches call the trials, where Tiffany's handling of the crisis is witnessed. Miss Level, gravely hurt during the ordeal, survives. Granny Weatherwax, who has tested and watched Tiffany throughout, grants her a rare and hard-won measure of respect, acknowledging her as a true witch. Tiffany returns to the Chalk having mastered both the hiver and herself, more fully aware of the responsibility and the power she carries.
recaps.in_short: Tiffany Aching, now eleven, leaves the Chalk to be trained as a witch, apprenticed to Miss Level, a kindly research witch who shares one mind between two bodies. Watched over from afar by the Feegle and by the formidable Granny Weatherwax, Tiffany learns the humble, practical work of a rural witch, but grows overconfident. An ancient, mindless predator called the hiver, drawn to powerful minds, catches and possesses her, and under its influence she becomes arrogant, cruel, and dangerous, no longer herself. The Nac Mac Feegle and Granny Weatherwax realize what has happened and set out to save her, and Miss Level is badly hurt in the crisis. Fighting back from within, Tiffany journeys into her own self to find the strength to master the thing that has taken her. At the great gathering of witches she finally defeats the hiver, not by force but by giving it what it has never had, an awareness of itself and of its own death, leading it at last to an ending. Tiffany comes fully into her own as a witch, earns Granny Weatherwax's hard-won respect, and returns to the Chalk stronger and surer of who she is.

recaps.text: Previously, in the earlier book: Tiffany Aching, a practical young granddaughter of a revered shepherd, discovered she had a talent for witchcraft on the chalk downland called the Chalk. When her small brother was stolen away by the Queen of Fairyland, Tiffany went into that cold country of dreams to rescue him, aided by the Nac Mac Feegle, the tiny, ferocious blue Wee Free Men who guard the downs and call her their hag. Drawing on clear sight, stubborn common sense, and the memory of her formidable grandmother, she saw through the Queen's illusions, defeated her, and brought the stolen children home. Senior witches, among them the renowned Granny Weatherwax, took note of what she had done. Recognized now as the Chalk's own young witch and set on the road to proper training, Tiffany has spent the time since learning what she can, with the Feegle still watching over her, and is ready to leave home for a real apprenticeship.

Tiffany leaves the Chalk and travels into the mountains to begin her formal training, apprenticed to Miss Level, a warm, unglamorous research witch who is remarkable for sharing a single mind between two separate bodies. Under her, Tiffany learns that real witchcraft is mostly hard, humble, practical work: tending the sick and the poor, doing the jobs no one else will, and quietly holding a scattered community together. It is a long way from the grand magic she imagined, and she is impatient with it. Meanwhile the Nac Mac Feegle, led by Rob Anybody and watched over by their sharp new kelda Jeannie, secretly follow Tiffany into the mountains to keep her safe, for Jeannie has sensed that something is coming. Unknown to Tiffany, an ancient and hungry thing is drifting toward her, drawn by the strength of her growing power.

Tiffany meets the local circle of young witch apprentices, including the domineering, image-obsessed Annagramma and the shy, kindly Petulia. She chafes at their preoccupation with the trappings and jargon of witchcraft, and, wanting to prove herself, grows overconfident about her own abilities and eager to show off her power. That pride leaves her exposed. The hiver, the ancient, mindless predator that has been closing in on her, seizes its moment and takes possession of her mind, drawn to her as the most powerful and tempting target it has found. With the thing riding inside her, Tiffany begins to change, and the danger she has walked into becomes clear both to the watching Feegle and to the wider world of witches.

Under the hiver's control, Tiffany becomes arrogant, careless, and cruel, using her power thoughtlessly and behaving in ways that are not her own. The possession makes her a danger to herself and to others. The Nac Mac Feegle, fiercely loyal, and Granny Weatherwax, who has been watching from a distance and grasps exactly what the hiver is, recognize what has happened and move to help her. In the turmoil Miss Level is gravely hurt. Tiffany, buried inside her own possessed mind, begins to fight back, struggling to find a foothold of self against the ancient thing that has swallowed her. It becomes clear that the hiver cannot be beaten by ordinary force, and that saving Tiffany will depend on Tiffany herself finding some deeper strength.

The struggle to free Tiffany from the hiver deepens, with Granny Weatherwax guiding and testing her and the Feegle lending their reckless courage. Tiffany learns that the hiver has no self of its own to attack, and that the answer lies not in fighting it but in understanding what it truly is: a mindless thing that has never known what it means to be someone. She journeys inward, into her own mind and into the strength she draws from her home ground and her sense of who she is, searching for a way to master the thing rather than merely resist it. All of this builds toward the great gathering of witches, the trials, where Tiffany will have to put what she has understood into practice and settle the matter for good.

Around the witches' gathering, Tiffany finally deals with the hiver. Rather than trying to destroy it, she draws it fully into herself and gives it the one thing it has never possessed: an awareness of being a self that can die. Made conscious of itself and of its own ending for the first time, the hiver is led to Death and finds the peace it never knew it lacked. Miss Level, badly hurt during the ordeal, survives. Granny Weatherwax, who has watched and tested Tiffany throughout, grants her a rare, hard-won respect and acknowledges her as a real witch. Having mastered both the ancient thing that took her and her own pride, Tiffany comes fully into her strength and her responsibilities. She returns home to the Chalk changed, surer of who she is and of the power she carries, a witch in her own right.

characters.description: The small, bookish heir of the Hairy Hooligans. Hiccup is poor at the loud parts of Viking life but can speak Dragonese, thinks carefully in a crisis and has survived several adventures by doing what nobody expects.
characters.name: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III

characters.description: Hiccup's tiny, selfish and frequently troublesome dragon. Toothless has no respect for books, rules or Hiccup's plans, although he does not like anyone else threatening his human.
characters.name: Toothless

characters.description: Hiccup's loyal, nervous friend, short-sighted and allergic to reptiles. Fishlegs shares Hiccup's low place in the training class and understands how badly an important test can go.
characters.name: Fishlegs

characters.description: Hiccup's Bog-Burglar friend, a bold and highly skilled thief. A forbidden building full of traps and locked doors sounds to Camicazi like a promising expedition.
characters.name: Camicazi

characters.description: Chief of the Hairy Hooligans and Hiccup's father. Stoick wants to be proud of his son but still measures heroism by the noisy standards of an old-fashioned Viking chief.
characters.name: Stoick the Vast

characters.description: The Hooligans' huge teacher and examiner, responsible for a training programme in which failure is painful and the instructions are generally shouted.
characters.name: Gobber the Belch

characters.description: Hiccup's boastful cousin and chief rival. Snotlout is strong, confident and ready to make sure everyone notices any part of the pirate test that Hiccup gets wrong.
characters.name: Snotface Snotlout

characters.description: Chief of the Bog-Burglars and Camicazi's mother, famous for her size, force of personality and valuable collection of stolen objects.
characters.name: Big-Boobied Bertha

characters.description: The terrifying guardian of the Meathead Public Library. He treats an overdue or stolen book as a serious crime and has dragons, rules and traps to enforce his authority.
characters.name: the Hairy Scary Librarian

characters.description: Dragons used to tunnel through the library's stonework and hunt intruders. Their ability to come through walls makes hiding among the shelves much harder.
characters.name: Driller-Dragons

characters.description: Hiccup's elderly grandfather and the Hooligans' soothsayer, a source of advice about old stories, unlikely signs and the parts of history other Vikings ignore.
characters.name: Old Wrinkly

recaps.ending: Hiccup, Fishlegs and Camicazi escape the Meathead Public Library with Toothless after surviving the Hairy Scary Librarian, his traps and the dragons that guard the collection. Hiccup saves knowledge that the librarian's rules would have kept locked away or destroyed, and the adventure gives him the understanding he needs to finish his own guide to dragons. He also makes it through the Viking testing surrounding his birthday, although not by turning into the large and violent hero the programme was designed to reward. The result is another victory for Hiccup's curiosity: books, careful observation and his ability to speak to dragons prove more useful than treating either books or dragons as enemies. He returns to his place among the Hooligans with his friends safe and with a growing written record of what he has learned about dragonkind.
recaps.in_short: On his birthday, Hiccup must face another stage of Gobber's Pirate Training Programme while also dealing with a book that has to go back to the forbidden Meathead Public Library. Hiccup, Fishlegs, Camicazi and Toothless break into the library, where books are guarded as dangerous treasures by the Hairy Scary Librarian and his dragons. Moving through traps, shelves and tunnels, Hiccup discovers that the knowledge kept there matters more than the rules meant to hide it. The Librarian hunts the children, and Driller-Dragons make the stone building itself unsafe. Hiccup escapes with his friends and saves the information he needs. He survives his birthday test without becoming the conventional hero his teachers expect, and his observations become part of his own guide to deadly dragons.

recaps.text: Previously: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III is the unlikely heir of the Hairy Hooligans. He is small, a poor fighter and much happier thinking than shouting, but he can secretly speak Dragonese. His dragon Toothless is tiny and disobedient; his closest friends are Fishlegs and Camicazi. Hiccup has saved Berk from giant sea dragons, Roman schemes, Alvin the Treacherous and a volcanic disaster. The last adventure also brought the famous Humungously Hotshot back to Tantrum O'Ugerly. Hiccup's tribe still expects its future chief to look like an ordinary Viking hero, while Hiccup keeps proving that knowledge and sympathy can be braver than an axe.

Hiccup's birthday arrives with very little peace or celebration. Gobber's Pirate Training Programme still expects him to pass dangerous tests designed for a much larger and louder boy, and Snotlout is ready to enjoy his failure. At the same time, a book connected with the Meathead Public Library has become Hiccup's responsibility. Books are not treated as harmless in this part of the Viking world, and the library is forbidden, heavily protected and run by a librarian whose punishments are legendary. Returning the book without being caught will require a different sort of test from the one Gobber has planned.

Hiccup enters the Meathead Public Library with Fishlegs, Camicazi and Toothless. The library is a maze of guarded shelves, locked passages and traps, with the Hairy Scary Librarian ready to punish intruders. Camicazi's skill with locks gets the children farther than Viking force could have done. Hiccup is drawn to the dragon knowledge hidden in the collection, but there is no time for quiet reading: Driller-Dragons can tunnel through the building and reach places that appear safe. The attempt to put one book right becomes a struggle to escape with both the children and important knowledge intact.

The Librarian closes in as the children move deeper through the library. Hiccup learns that the books contain observations about dragons that his tribe has forgotten or refuses to consider. He cannot simply abandon that knowledge, even though Toothless and the Driller-Dragons keep making the escape more difficult. Outside the library, the demands of his pirate training have not disappeared, so Hiccup must solve two problems at once: get his friends out of a place designed to hold intruders and still face the test waiting for him among the Hooligans.

Hiccup, Fishlegs, Camicazi and Toothless escape the Meathead Public Library after outwitting the Hairy Scary Librarian and surviving the dragons that guard it. Hiccup preserves the useful dragon lore he has found rather than allowing fear and strict rules to bury it. He also comes through the Viking testing attached to his birthday, not because he suddenly becomes stronger than Snotlout, but because he notices, learns and acts under pressure. The adventure feeds into Hiccup's own work of recording dragon species and their dangers. His guide becomes evidence that understanding dragons is a form of heroism, even if Gobber's lessons do not have a mark for it.

characters.description: The narrator: a retired Circus officer, half Breton and half Scottish, who spent his career in the field and in Smiley's service and now lives on his mother's farm in Brittany with his companion Catherine and her daughter. Old, careful with money and content to be forgotten, he is summoned to London by a letter from a Service he no longer recognises, and finds that the past he helped to bury has been dug up.
characters.name: Peter Guillam

characters.description: Guillam's chief now: the head of the Circus in his time, and the man who devised and ran the operations now under investigation. He has long since disappeared from public life, and nobody at the modern Service will say where he is.
characters.name: George Smiley

characters.description: The Frenchwoman who farms Guillam's land in Brittany and shares his house, direct, unsentimental and incurious about his past, with a daughter who does not speak.
characters.name: Catherine

characters.description: The Service's lawyer, courteous, quick and entirely modern, who conducts the interviews. His concern is not with what was right but with what can be defended in front of a parliamentary committee and a court, and with making sure the Service of today is not held responsible for the Service of fifty years ago.
characters.name: Bunny

characters.description: The Service's in-house historian and researcher, who has read the surviving files more thoroughly than anyone alive and has noticed exactly which documents are missing. Sharp, hostile and impatient with the old men's evasions, she conducts much of the questioning.
characters.name: Laura

characters.description: A Circus officer of the fifties and sixties, hard, solitary and a heavy drinker, who ran the Berlin station and its agents into East Germany. He is spoken of in the files and by everyone who knew him as the best field man of his generation, and he has been dead for decades.
characters.name: Alec Leamas

characters.description: A young London librarian and communist party member who became attached to Leamas, and who died with him at the Berlin Wall. She had no part in the intelligence world beyond the use that was made of her.
characters.name: Liz Gold

characters.description: Leamas's son by a marriage that failed, brought up in Germany and grown into a hard, damaged and unscrupulous man with convictions behind him. He wants money and he wants somebody punished, and he is prepared to threaten in order to get both.
characters.name: Christoph Leamas

characters.description: The operations chief of the East German service, feared and detested by his own colleagues, a physically cold and violent man with an unsavoury war record. During the period under investigation he was also the Circus's most productive source, recruited in London after an operation went wrong and protected at enormous cost.
characters.name: Hans-Dieter Mundt

characters.description: The Circus's code name for Doris Gamp, an East German woman married to a Stasi officer, who volunteered her services to the West out of anger and conviction rather than money. Devout, headstrong and physically brave, she photographed documents from inside the service that employed her husband and became for a time the Circus's best window into it. She has a young son she is obliged to leave behind.
characters.name: Tulip

characters.description: The head of the Circus during the period under investigation, secretive, ill and manipulative, who conceived the operations at the centre of the enquiry and never told any one participant more than a fraction of the whole. He died shortly after they ended.
characters.name: Control

characters.description: Liz Gold's daughter, brought up by relatives and told very little about her mother's death. She is educated, temperate and genuinely in search of the truth rather than damages, which makes her harder to deal with than her fellow claimant.
characters.name: Karen Gold

characters.description: A Scottish Circus veteran who kept the service's safe houses and their secrets for decades, still alive, still discreet, and still loyal to the men she worked for. What she remembers about a particular house in the country is not what the files record.
characters.name: Millie McCraig

recaps.ending: The inquiry ends with the Service intending to settle: the claimants will be paid off, the record will be tidied, and the responsibility will rest where it can do the modern Service least harm, which means on Guillam and on men who are dead. Guillam, having told as much of the truth as he judges the dead can bear and having been threatened by Christoph Leamas along the way, leaves London rather than wait for the verdict, and goes to Germany to find Smiley. He finds him very old, in a library in Freiburg, still reading, unrepentant and precise. Smiley confirms what Guillam had worked out: Mundt was the Circus's agent, Windfall existed to protect him, Tulip died at his hands and the Circus concealed it, and Leamas and Liz Gold were expended in the same cause without being told. Asked what it was all for, Smiley says he did it for his service and his country while he believed in them, and that if there was a cause beyond that it was Europe. He offers no defence beyond the fact that the choices were made by men who knew what they cost. Guillam goes back to Brittany, the past acknowledged and nothing about it repaired.
recaps.in_short: Peter Guillam, long retired to a farm in Brittany, is summoned to London by the modern Service. The children of Alec Leamas and Liz Gold, who died at the Berlin Wall decades earlier, are suing, and a parliamentary committee wants an account of the operations that killed them. Questioned by the Service's lawyer Bunny and its historian Laura, and confronted with files he helped to write and to weed, Guillam recalls the Berlin operations of the fifties and sixties: the East German network, and its best source, a woman code-named Tulip, the wife of a Stasi officer, whom Guillam helped to exfiltrate through Prague and with whom he fell in love. Tulip was murdered soon after reaching England, and the Circus buried it, because her killer was Mundt, the East German operations chief who was also the Circus's own agent. Everything that followed, including the operation that destroyed Leamas and Liz Gold, existed to keep Mundt in place. Threatened by Leamas's son and set up as the Service's scapegoat, Guillam finally tracks down George Smiley in Freiburg and hears him account for it all.

recaps.text: Previously: Alec Leamas, head of the Circus's Berlin station in the early nineteen sixties, lost his last agent at a checkpoint and was sent by Control on a final operation. He played out a public ruin into drink, debt and prison, was recruited by East German talent-spotters and taken East, where his information was used by Jens Fiedler, the East German counter-intelligence chief, to accuse his own operations chief, Hans-Dieter Mundt, of working for London. At a secret tribunal, Mundt's advocate produced Liz Gold, a young London librarian who had become Leamas's lover and had been brought East on a party exchange, and her truthful evidence exposed Leamas's defection as a British operation. Fiedler was destroyed and Mundt cleared. Mundt then released Leamas and Liz, because Mundt was in fact the Circus's own agent and the whole operation had been designed to protect him by removing the one man closing in on him. At the Wall, Liz was shot by the guards and Leamas climbed back down to die beside her. Peter Guillam was a junior officer in the Circus at the time, and George Smiley was Control's closest colleague.

Peter Guillam, long retired from the Circus, lives on his mother's farm in Brittany with Catherine, who works the land, and her daughter. A letter from the Service he served for forty years asks him, in terms he cannot refuse, to come to London. He is received in a glass building on the river by Bunny, a Service lawyer, and Laura, its in-house historian, and told what has happened: the children of Alec Leamas and Liz Gold are bringing a civil action over the deaths of their parents at the Berlin Wall, and a parliamentary committee is preparing to examine the operations that led to them. The Service wants an account of two old operations, Mayflower and Windfall, before it is given one by somebody else. Guillam is required to read documents he helped to create, some of which he knows to be false and some of which are missing, and to explain them under questioning by people who were not born when the events occurred.

Through the files and Guillam's own memory, the Berlin story is reassembled. In the years when the Wall was going up, the Circus was running an East German network from West Berlin, with Alec Leamas in charge of the field work and Control and Smiley directing from London. The network's best material came from a woman code-named Tulip: Doris Gamp, the wife of a Stasi officer, who offered herself to the West out of conviction and photographed documents from inside her husband's service. Her product was so good that London built a special handling arrangement around it. Guillam, then a young officer, was drawn into her case. It becomes clear from the surviving papers that only Control and Smiley knew what the material was really being used for, and that Leamas and Guillam were being told a version of the operation designed to keep them convincing rather than informed.

Tulip's position becomes untenable and she has to be brought out. Guillam escorts her through Czechoslovakia on a difficult exfiltration, sleeping in safe rooms and moving on false papers, and in the course of it they become lovers; she leaves her young son behind. She is landed in England and housed at a Circus safe house in the country, kept from the world and impatient at being idle. Within a short time she is dead, killed at the house, and the Circus disposes of the matter without a police enquiry and without telling the agents who had risked their lives for her. Guillam was told a story about it that he half believed at the time. The modern Service's researchers have found the gaps in that story, and their questions are directed at what Guillam knew, what he wrote and what he later removed from the file.

The pressure on Guillam comes from two directions. In London, Bunny and Laura shift from asking him to explain the past to preparing him to carry it: the Service means to settle the claim and needs a name to attach to the deaths, and the men who gave the orders are dead.
